newsitem.title: USA: Service Corp. extends Loewen offer. [CORRECTED 09:45 GMT 02/11]
newsitem.headline: Service Corp. extends Loewen offer. [CORRECTED 09:45 GMT 02/11]

text.p: Service Corp. International said Friday that it has extended the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period in connection with its exchange offer for all outstanding shares of Loewen Group Inc. (Corrects to clarify what waiting period refers to by adding "the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period".)
Service Corp. said the Federal Trade Commission has asked for more information with respect to its antitrust filings.
The company said that the waiting period, which was originally scheduled to expire Nov. 2, will be extended and now expire 20 days after it complies with the FTC request.
Service Corp., is the world's largest funeral home and cemetery organisation.
Loewen, the Vancouver, British Columbia-based funeral company, also said it has received a second request for information from the FTC in connection the hostile takeover proposal from Service Corp.
On Oct. 1, the FTC requested data on all of the Loewen Group's funeral homes and cemeteries, including all properties in which the company has a financial interest.
Loewen, the second biggest operator of funeral homes and cemeteries in North America, has rejected the bid by Service Corp.

Loewen has sought to highlight potential anti-trust obstacles to the deal. Houston-based Service has said it believes any anti-trust concerns can be overcome by disposing of a limited number of properties.
Loewen previously announced that nine U.S. states, the FTC and Canada's competition bureau were probing the offer.
It said the FTC's second request for information also covers Loewen's Prime Succession Inc. unit and Equity Corp. International, which is 40 percent owned by Service Corp.
